source_title: Jamie Chung Lost Atlanta Home 1 Year After Escaping California Fires (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actress and her family were among those who lost their homes in the California fires in January 2025
Jamie Chung reveals to PEOPLE that her family’s home in Atlanta burned down over the summer, one year after they were affected by the California wildfires
The actress says she’s learned to stay calm through it all and shared how her children help keep her grounded
Chung stars in The Holiday Spark , premiering Nov. 2 on The Roku Channel
Jamie Chung , 40, is learning all about crisis management.
A year after she and husband, Bryan Greenberg, lost their home in the California wildfires that ravaged the Pacific Palisades, Pasadena, Altadena and more areas in January 2025, the actress revealed her family was also evacuated from their Atlanta home after it caught fire this past summer.
“There was a big fire on the roof and a lot of people evacuated,” she told PEOPLE ahead of her keynote appearance at StyleWeekOC in partnership with the Newport Beach Film Festival, on Oct. 16. “My apartment’s unlivable at the moment, but that’s to be expected.”
The actress was in town filming her upcoming holiday movie, The Holiday Spark, when the fire happened, and though everyone is safe, she admitted the ordeal was a lot to manage.
“It was just quite traumatic having to deal with all that again,” she revealed. “And it wasn’t as bad, luckily. No one was hurt, no one was killed. That’s what matters.”
Looking at the silver lining, Chung revealed that she and Greenberg have gotten closer throughout the ordeal and she’s learned she’s the better half when it comes to crisis management. “Honestly, I’m the one that’s better with logistics when it comes to a crisis that we’ve experienced. And I think the trick is to absolutely stay calm, to focus on what matters the most, which is our family and our health, and being present,” she said.
“I feel like when the fires happened in Altadena, I lost focus of what was important and I got so overwhelmed by the logistics, the paperwork. Getting all my paperwork in order, dealing with the insurance, talking to lawyers, other fire victims,” she continued.
“Reading fun, case studies on the neighborhood that we purchased in and how it used to be cattle ranches, and third-party fire self-defense, off-the-grid systems that I can potentially look towards, architects. The list is ongoing and the amount of support that was given to me in the beginning was so generous from previous fire victims and lawyers and whatnot.”
Their 5-year-old twin boys have also been a source of comfort for the star, as she said they remind her about the bigger picture. “They certainly kept me grounded and present, but grounded in a way like you’re not spinning out with anxiety and wondering about the what ifs and whatnot. Really being grounded and present, enjoying this moment of learning how to read or telling funny joke. I think those kind of things are way more important,” she stated.
Come Nov. 2, Chung will be ushering in the holiday cheer with The Holiday Spark , which will be available for free on The Roku Channel. Costarring former Bachelor Joey Graziadei , the movie follows “perpetually single firefighter Dean (Graziadei), who enlists children’s book illustrator Laura (Chung) to help plan his firehouse’s most unforgettable holiday party yet. Throughout the planning process, they both begin to question their views on romance and the possibility of love at first spark,” per The Roku Channel.
